intuition.title: Study context: Reductive route
intuition.text: The authors propose that Mg reduces WO3 and ethanol to reactive W and C, followed by carbide formation. Equations describe a proposed mechanism; intermediate yields were not measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Equations 1–7 and mechanism discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Filling comparison
intuition.text: Higher ethanol filling correlates with fewer other tungsten phases in the source XRD series. The paper attributes this to system pressure without giving pressure measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Filling discussion and Figure 2

intuition.title: Study context: Carbon coating
intuition.text: Excess carbon is proposed to deposit on WC surfaces. Both carbon-coated and carbon-free particles are observed; no uniform coating or population fraction is claimed.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and mechanism discussion

scopeLabel: Complete supplied two-page main, Figures 1–3, equations 1–7 and all 16 references. SI and cited full sources unreviewed. One fully quantified main procedure. WC and carbon-bearing/carbon-free populations are source-linked, without inventing separate batches or coated fractions. Independent source comparison passed; presentation pending.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Load 1.5 g WO3, 1 g Mg and 12 mL anhydrous ethanol into a 16 mL stainless-steel autoclave. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Seal the autoclave. No initial gas atmosphere, pressure or liner material is reported. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Place the sealed autoclave in the furnace at 100 °C. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Increase the furnace temperature from 100 to 600 °C over 50 min; internal specimen temperature is not separately measured. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Maintain the furnace at 600 °C for 15 h with the autoclave sealed. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Allow the autoclave to cool to room temperature; cooling duration is unreported. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Collect the dark solid powder; the collection method and recovered mass are unreported. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Wash the collected solid with dilute HCl to remove unreacted Mg. Concentration, volume and contact time are not supplied. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Wash the acid-treated solid with distilled water and ethanol to remove by-products. Volumes, cycles and separation method are unreported. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Typical experimental procedure, continued in right column
bindings.caption: Dry the washed product under vacuum at 50 °C for 10 h; numerical vacuum pressure is unreported. Geometry is original conceptual equipment, not measured source apparatus.

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
